tweets.textSnippet: Five things I’ve done in my first week
It most certainly is, Ed. Let’s work together to find some common ground.

I'm used to people telling me things can't be done.

I didn't accept it then. I won't accept it now.

It's time to get Britain believing again and bring back hope.

This week is just the start.
Across the country people want to see change for the better.

The wildfire in the Cairngorms has been raging for 10 days and it has been devastating for the families and communities living nearby.

Huge thanks to the Fire and Rescue Service, the Police and the many volunteers working round the clock to protect life and property.

This has to be the start of a real effort to end the social care catastrophe. 


@AndyBurnham
 says he’s willing to spend political capital on this - and so am I. 

I’ll fight to ensure family carers aren't forgotten. We need cross-party consensus, and I hope the PM’s door is ope

The Telegraph front page reports Iran is smuggling its operatives into Britain via the English Channel. 

I have been warning about this since April.

Labour’s own MPs shouted “shame on you” when I warned about Iran. 

The truth is, it’s shame on them. 

They are endangering British lives by letting terrorists in.

This coming Thursday.

Let's make it happen.

Vote Green as your first preference vote.

Let's take Greater Manchester back from private profit and run it for the people.

Terrorising communities. 

Splitting up families. 

These are political choices that Burnham is backing by reappointing Shabana Mahmood in the Home Office. 

These are choices the Green Party will always fight.

Brilliant to meet with Thomas Piketty at the Paris School of Economics.

We discussed monetary and fiscal policy, bond markets, the climate crisis and global wealth taxes.

Also recorded a podcast for 
@_BoldPolitics
 - out soon!

Terrifying to see wildfires raging through Scotland.

The climate crisis isn't a distant threat - it's right here and right now.

How many warning signs and alarm bells until Andy Burnham takes action to end oil and gas drilling?

Goldsmith ran one of the most racist campaigns in British political history and London rejected him. 

Our twinning proposal is about offering practical and moral support to a city subjugated under a brutal military occupation. 

He remains ignorant to this by his own prejudice.
Sending all my love and solidarity to Berlin.

Thanks WOMAD - that was so uplifting today!

Amazing to see so many people in the tent - and a huge overflow too.

People want rent controls, wealth taxes and action to tackle the climate crisis.
